## Definitions

- [statement] SERVER-124090, updated October 23, 2026, is an unresolved improvement with no fix version. It specifies x-mongodb-searchnodepreference as xxHash64(searchNodePreference.key), alongside command and shard headers, and requests equivalent metadata for legacy aggregate, planShardedSearch, and search-cursor getMore paths. This describes engineering requirements for fallback routing, not proof that a particular released version implements them. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-124090 · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency

## Structure and components

- [statement] Affinity improves potential result consistency without guaranteeing permanent consistency. MongoDB explicitly lists changes in the dataset, index structure, cluster topology, and preferred-node availability as causes of remaining inconsistencies. Treating the key as a frozen result snapshot would exceed the documented guarantee. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md

## How it works

- [statement] A practical consequence of the documented affinity contract is to reuse the same preference key for a sequence of related requests when repeatability matters. Changing the key removes that sequence's stated same-value routing condition; keeping it still does not freeze the underlying results. This is application guidance inferred from the contract. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/query-ref.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Percona's October 1, 2026 $vectorSearch reference includes searchNodePreference: {key: <preference-string>} in its syntax, but its field table does not explain affinity semantics. It corroborates the parameter shape in a separate implementation context, not Atlas availability, failure behavior, or consistency guarantees. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-search-for-mongodb/query-vector-search.html · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Routing affinity does not remove the usual result-fetching stage: mongot returns matching document IDs and metadata, and mongod normally looks up the documents. The separate returnStoredSource option controls returning stored fields instead of the backend document lookup. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/query-ref.md · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The $search stage accepts the optional object searchNodePreference: {key: <arbitrary string>}. Keeping the key value unchanged preferentially routes repeated queries to the same search node and overrides default search-node routing. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/query-ref.md
- [statement] With separate mongod and mongot nodes, read preference first selects mongod. By default mongod sends the search through its local load balancer across mongot processes; searchNodePreference changes search-node routing at this second step. These are distinct routing controls. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/query-ref.md · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md
- [statement] The related $vectorSearch syntax also includes searchNodePreference with a key string in both MongoDB and Percona documentation. Percona documents its own product syntax; this does not independently establish Atlas routing or result-consistency behavior. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md · keywords: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-search-for-mongodb/query-vector-search.html
